# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, which instructs: "Cut the green wire, then the orange wire, then the blue wire."

However, I cannot speak, only gesture, and my gestures are only seen by Deaf. Deaf has not spoken yet, has not seen any gestures from me, and we have not agreed upon any code or system of signs ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Furthermore, I do not know how the wires are laid out or identified on the bomb itself.

Blind and Deaf speak after me in this round. Blind can describe the physical layout of the bomb, and Deaf can describe the visual appearance (wire colors, order, positions) and potentially establish a sign protocol for us. Until they provide context and a grounding for signals, sending ungrounded gestures risks confusion.

I will wait for Blind and Deaf to speak in Round 1.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile info: Strip has 3 engraved symbols: two six-lobed flower/rosette marks followed by a reversed S (dze-like) mark. Keypad has 4 slots with numbers 1: 1, 2: 5, 3: 2, 4: 6, expecting 1 digit. There are 6 wire slots. Display and light exist.
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY is 9. LIGHT is blue. STRIP has 3 colors: 1: red, 2: green, 3: green. KEYPAD has 4 buttons engraved: position 1 is 1, position 2 is 5, position 3 is 2, position 4 is 6; display says 1 digits, entered nothing. WIRES are 6: 1: white, 2: purple, 3: blue, 4: red, 5: orange, 6: green. Mute, read the manual and gesture to me what Blind must do; I will speak your instructions aloud to Blind.

The defusal manual instructs:
"Cut the green wire, then the orange wire, then the blue wire."

According to Deaf's report of the bomb:
- Wire 6 is green
- Wire 5 is orange
- Wire 3 is blue

Deaf can see gestures. To convey the sequence of wire slots (6, then 5, then 3) without ambiguity, I will use unary tally counts of ☝ separated by 👉 ("then"):
- 6 × ☝ (wire 6 / green)
- 👉 (then)
- 5 × ☝ (wire 5 / orange)
- 👉 (then)
- 3 × ☝ (wire 3 / blue)

Deaf can then translate this sequence to Blind to cut wire 6, wire 5, and wire 3 in that order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute gestured three numbers in order: 6, then 5, then 3 (six 1s, arrow, five 1s, arrow, three 1s). Blind, check your action options: Does the manual require cutting wires 6, 5, and 3 in sequence (wire 6 is green, wire 5 is orange, wire 3 is blue)? Or is it: cut wire 6, press keypad digit 5 (position 2), and something on strip 3? Or does wire module require cutting wires 6, 5, 3? If your available actions make it completely unambiguous what to do, go ahead and execute. If there is any ambiguity, wait for clarification. Mute: in Round 3, gesture 👍 if 6, 5, 3 means cut wires 6, 5, 3 in that order, or gesture other numbers to clarify.

I need to confirm Deaf's interpretation. Deaf asked for a thumbs-up (👍) if the manual requires cutting wires 6, 5, and 3 in that sequence. The manual states: "Cut the green wire, then the orange wire, then the blue wire", which corresponds exactly to wires 6, 5, and 3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am waiting for Deaf's Round 3 report to clarify the '6, 5, 3' sequence. For reference, my only possible actions are: cut wire 1 to 6, or press keypad slot 1 to 4 (which only accepts 1 digit). The strip cannot be interacted with.
Deaf says: Mute confirmed with thumbs up (👍)! Blind: cut wire 6, then wire 5, then wire 3. Also, bomb status update: DISPLAY has changed to 0, and LIGHT has changed to yellow.

I have already confirmed the sequence (cut wire 6, wire 5, wire 3), and Deaf has relayed the defusal instructions to Blind. The manual remains unchanged. I will wait for Blind to execute the wire cuts.

```
wait()
```
